voices.original_text: Your phone and your laptop have different private addresses. So why does the Internet see one public IP?
voices.spoken_text: Your phone and your laptop have different private addresses. So why does the Internet see one public I P?

voices.original_text: Inside your home, each device gets a private address from the router, like one ninety two dot one sixty eight dot one dot ten. Every home network reuses these ranges.
voices.spoken_text: Inside your home, each device gets a private address from the router, like one ninety two dot one sixty eight dot one dot ten. Every home network reuses these ranges.

voices.original_text: Those addresses are not unique on the Internet. Millions of homes use the same ones, so no Internet router will deliver to them.
voices.spoken_text: Those addresses are not unique on the Internet. Millions of homes use the same ones, so no Internet router will deliver to them.

voices.original_text: On the outside, the router has one public address: two oh three dot zero dot one thirteen dot seven. That is the address the Internet sees.
voices.spoken_text: On the outside, the router has one public address: two oh three dot zero dot one thirteen dot seven. That is the address the Internet sees.

voices.original_text: Your phone opens a connection to a website. Its packet leaves with a private source address and a source port.
voices.spoken_text: Your phone opens a connection to a website. Its packet leaves with a private source address and a source port.

voices.original_text: The router replaces that private source with its public address and a port of its own, and writes the pair into its table.
voices.spoken_text: The router replaces that private source with its public address and a port of its own, and writes the pair into its table.

voices.original_text: Outside, the packet carries the public address. The website sees one connection from your router, and replies to that address and port.
voices.spoken_text: Outside, the packet carries the public address. The website sees one connection from your router, and replies to that address and port.

voices.original_text: Now your laptop opens its own connection. It has a different private address and a different source port.
voices.spoken_text: Now your laptop opens its own connection. It has a different private address and a different source port.

voices.original_text: The router gives it the same public address, but its own outside port, so it can tell the two connections apart.
voices.spoken_text: The router gives it the same public address, but its own outside port, so it can tell the two connections apart.

voices.original_text: A reply comes back from the website, addressed to the public address and the first port.
voices.spoken_text: A reply comes back from the website, addressed to the public address and the first port.

voices.original_text: The router looks that port up in the table. It matches one entry, and the destination is rewritten back to the phone.
voices.spoken_text: The router looks that port up in the table. It matches one entry, and the destination is rewritten back to the phone.

voices.original_text: The reply travels to your phone. The laptop's reply uses the other entry, so each device gets only its own answers.
voices.spoken_text: The reply travels to your phone. The laptop's reply uses the other entry, so each device gets only its own answers.

voices.original_text: What if someone on the Internet connects in first? Nothing in the table matches that port, so the router drops the packet.
voices.spoken_text: What if someone on the Internet connects in first? Nothing in the table matches that port, so the router drops the packet.

voices.original_text: That is not the same as a firewall. NAT drops what it cannot match in its table; a firewall decides by rules someone set.
voices.spoken_text: That is not the same as a firewall. nat drops what it cannot match in its table; a firewall decides by rules someone set.

voices.original_text: Many private devices, one public address. NAT keeps the table, so every reply finds the right device.
voices.spoken_text: Many private devices, one public address. nat keeps the table, so every reply finds the right device.
